cards.anchor: Produce three elevation samples with attenuation spread at most 4 percent at second 120, using less stirring if feasible. One stipulated 300 rpm, 60-second run already met this bounded proxy; repeat reliability remains hypothetical.
cards.burden: Allocate two of the six fresh-recipe trials to replication. Each requires 60 stirring seconds, a 60-second quiet interval, five-second image logging and three depth withdrawals. Actual savings relative to the preferred procedure remain unknown.
cards.construction: In each trial use 150 mL water and 0.30 mL dye in the rinsed beaker, with the same bottle, addition location and locked camera. Command 300 rpm for exactly 60 seconds; stop regardless of optical spread and never restart before second-120 sampling. Withdraw 1 mL at 10, 28 and 45 mm within ten seconds, reversing depth order between trials. Use water and common-aliquot references, spill tray, and stop on liquid escape.
cards.defeat: Any valid replicate with final spread above 4 percent defeats a claim that this fixed recipe reliably meets the target in every trial. Consistent depth-order dependence weakens a bulk-uniformity interpretation. Neither result proves 900 rpm necessary.
cards.mutation: Replace optical stabilization as the duration controller with a precommitted lower-speed dose and a separate final-sample acceptance decision.
cards.prediction_candidate: Hypothesis: both fresh repeats meet the final-vial target even when side images fail the preferred rule, supporting bounded repeatability without sustained 900 rpm.
cards.prediction_rival: Hypothesis: final-vial spread exceeds 4 percent in repeats, or reversing sampling order systematically changes apparent spread, indicating residual gradients or sampling-mediated success.
cards.probe: Execute both fixed interventions without feedback rescue. Compare raw final readings and normalized spread across reversed sampling orders; log side spread and duration independently. Two trials provide weak evidence about reliability and cannot establish systematic order effects.
cards.rival: The earlier success was exceptional or sampling-mediated; repeated fixed low-speed mixing leaves gradients.
unknowns: Reference repeatability is not concentration calibration; sampling may disturb gradients.
Two repetitions cannot establish broad reliability or transfer to other recipes.
No matched preferred-rule duration establishes time savings.

cards.anchor: Retain the same second-120 final-vial spread target of at most 4 percent while testing whether optical control adds stirring without sample benefit. Future 900 rpm timer-stop success is a hypothesis.
cards.burden: Use the remaining four trials as two fresh matched pairs, reversing enabled/timer trial order between pairs. Together with the first card this exactly uses the six-trial, 90-minute budget. Record all durations and failures; limited replication and unequal quiet intervals restrict causal attribution.
cards.construction: Within each pair hold recipe, bottle, addition location, camera and references fixed. One run commands 900 rpm until three consecutive five-second image checks are at most 4 percent, with mandatory stop by second 105. The other commands 900 rpm for exactly 60 seconds, logs the same rule in shadow mode, and cannot restart. Sample both at second 120 using the three marked depths; alternate sampling order. Keep the spill tray in use and stop on escape.
cards.defeat: Repeated timer-target failure with enabled-target success defeats the claim that severing optical control preserves this outcome in these pairs. If enabled runs use no more stirring, the proposed duration benefit is absent. Both-run failures or inconsistent results leave the comparison unresolved.
cards.mutation: Sever the optical-spread-to-stirring command link while retaining its decisions as an observational shadow and keeping nominal speed fixed.
cards.prediction_candidate: Hypothesis: timer runs meet the vial target despite shadow-rule failures; enabled runs also meet it but stir longer than 60 seconds. This would support dispensability of extra feedback-driven stirring in these pairs.
cards.prediction_rival: Hypothesis: timer runs retain final spread above 4 percent while longer enabled runs meet the target, favoring useful additional mixing under the comparison conditions.
cards.probe: Compare final-vial spread, actual total stirring and cessation times within both reversed-order pairs. Log side frames before and after cessation and shadow decisions. A prompt image change can support an agitation-to-image effect but cannot identify specks or establish a disturbance-renewal loop.
cards.rival: Real unresolved gradients produce image spread, and additional agitation improves the sample outcome.
unknowns: The disturbance-renewal return loop and speck identity remain unobserved hypotheses; no bubble measurement is available.
Different cessation times mean different quiet intervals before sampling; outcome differences cannot be attributed solely to stirring.
Sampling disturbance, nominal speed and uncalibrated optical measures constrain interpretation.
No conclusion extends beyond this synthetic bounded proxy.
